On Starship’s 15th flight last week, the Super Heavy booster correctly performed a safe abort when returning for a catch and ended its mission with a splashdown in the water off the coast of Starbase. Following splashdown, SpaceX recovery teams were immediately onsite to safe the area while our Environmental Health and Safety team worked to ensure any debris that washes onshore was recovered → http://x.com/SpaceX/status/2121629958036492590

When we received reports of potential debris in Mexican territory, we immediately mobilized to send specialists to aid in identification and lead any cleanup work required, just as we did on Boca Chica Beach near Starbase. We continue to stay in contact with the Mexican government and are on standby to send support if authorities in Mexico tell us it is actually needed. Partners on the ground relayed that theyhave found very little debris in their sweeps of the beach, and the small amount they have found are not clearly from SpaceX operations.

The majority of the social media posts online claiming widespread debris and damage are either outright fabrications or intentionally misleading. As repeatedly stated, independent tests conducted on materials inside Starship and the Super Heavy booster, including toxicity analyses, confirm they pose no chemical, biological, or toxicological risks.

Starship is designed to be fully reusable, with future missions planning to return all hardware back to the launch site for catch and reuse. SpaceX is the only one, whether company or country, that has demonstrated this capability is now possible.

Elon Musk explains why SpaceX catching Starship achieves the "holy grail of rocketry," and can cut the cost of access to space by 100x:

In 2025, SpaceX launched 2,200 tons to orbit, more than 80% of the global total.

Elon Musk's goal with Starship is 1,000,000 tons to orbit per year, about 450x what SpaceX launched last year.

Falcon 9 reuses its booster but throws away the upper stage on every flight. Starship is designed to bring back both.

"We've had three booster catches, but this is the first ship catch, which means we've now at least proven that all parts of Starship can be flown to space and recovered in good enough shape to be reflown."

"No one has ever taken a stage like that and created a truly reusable upper stage, and certainly not brought it back and had it land propulsively while being caught by giant chopsticks, which sounds like some kind of preposterous sci-fi book or something. But it's done."

"Starship can drop the cost of access to space by a factor of 100... and achieve a mass to orbit rate that is in the million ton per year range."

"This has been the holy grail of rocketry from the beginning, to have a fully reusable rocket system."

"The Space Shuttle was partially reusable, but the main tank… was thrown away on every flight… The shuttle orbiter, the plane-like thing, would take something like nine months to refurbish between flights."

"Whereas Starship is designed for complete reusability and to be reused immediately like an airplane. The booster lands, you can put another ship on top and take off immediately."

"The net effect of this, to put it into economic terms, is a hundredfold reduction in the cost of access to space, and maybe even eventually a thousandfold reduction."

"That's what's necessary in order to make life multiplanetary, in order to build a city on the Moon or Mars… You couldn't do it even if you had the whole budget of the United States government."

Elon Musk and SpaceX have been working toward a fully reusable orbital rocket for more than two decades.

Five days ago, they proved every part of Starship can fly to space and be recovered.

quote.author: firesidealpha

quote.text:
Dario Amodei says Anthropic could drive at 200 miles an hour but chooses 90

“So this is one of the central tensions at the heart of the company, but it’s really because this technology is so powerful, it has so many effects in the world. It’s something that every company in this space will have to face, whether they want to or not. We’re just facing it more explicitly and more thoughtfully. And so you think about something like pacing.”

“The idea behind pacing was, imagine that you’re driving your car at 60 miles an hour, and then you discover or invent something that could let you drive the car at 200 miles an hour. This is models building themselves, recursive self-improvement. What we’ve done with pacing is essentially said, look, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let’s only drive at 90 miles an hour. Spend time figuring out how to do that safely, and the rest of that surplus, we spend building the model in the right way.”

“And I think in the long run, that will work out pretty well for the investors as well, because the company that builds the safest, that has the trust of the customers and the enterprises of the world, I think that is the company that’s going to be both best for society and, in the long run, I hope, best for the performance of the company.”

posts.text:
Elon gave two talks today at DealBook and TomorrowX Summit, revealing more about SpaceX's plans than most earnings calls. Here are the 11 key takeaways:

1. SpaceX is scaling AI compute at an extraordinary pace:

SpaceX is adding roughly 500 MW monthly, equivalent to 220,000 GB300s. Elon expects over 1 GW monthly by end-2027: a 6 GW annualized pace today, doubling to 12 GW. 

2. Its build costs are far below industry estimates:

Elon says outside estimates are off by up to 2x, with SpaceX building at roughly 60% of industry costs. Its in-house "Army X" builds the data centers, while Tesla Megapacks smooth training power. I'd already been modeling a 25–30% SpaceX cost advantage. 

3. Anthropic could become a 10 GW customer:

Anthropic told Elon its most likely outcome is renting another 10 GW from SpaceX, on top of existing capacity. Contracts allow termination with 3–6 months' notice, but Anthropic says staying is "extremely likely." This reinforces my model that Anthropic will take most upcoming capacity.

4. SpaceX is targeting a vastly larger telecom market:

Elon argues AT&T and Verizon won't disappear as bandwidth demand explodes. Humans communicate at roughly 100 bits per second, while superintelligence and robots could require a trillion. SpaceX is targeting a market orders of magnitude larger than existing telecom revenue, as I'd modeled. Even more interestingly, this creates an opportunity to push its AI business further.

5. Its next-generation satellite network arrives next year:

Direct to Cell V2 launches with 40x V1's bandwidth. Micro cell towers using 800 MHz and rooftop units resembling Starlink dishes will extend indoor coverage, with rooftop hardware entering production next year. Starlink is becoming a full scale carrier. 

6. SpaceXSI has rebuilt its entire AI software stack:

Over six to eight months, it rewrote training, reinforcement learning, and inference from scratch, close to the metal in C and C++. Elon thinks it "might have the best training stack software in the world." Grok 4.8 is also being built for practical usefulness rather than benchmark leadership, which is great for Grokbot.

7. Terafab could become the largest project on Earth:

The facility is planned to reach 100 million square feet, with phase-one volume production targeted for late 2028. Elon says established chipmakers are risk-averse because of massive capex, while SpaceX will take risks and iterate rapidly toward a better chip process by 2028.

8. Optimus is moving toward industrial work:

Elon expects an unstaged demonstration in a month or two and says Optimus could do dishes within 12–18 months. Its first major industrial role will be mining and refining ore for national security.

9. A Tesla–SpaceX merger is becoming increasingly logical:

Elon says the companies are "probably" better together as AI and robotics bring them closer. Both have AI software teams and advanced chip-design capabilities, while superintelligence compute could eventually move into orbit. Shareholders will decide; Elon says he shouldn't receive an award simply for merging them.

10. Ship 42 could accelerate the entire Starship reuse program:

Ship 42 needed only minor repairs before flying again, but SpaceX is retiring it for public display. This brings rapid reuse much closer.

11. SpaceX is targeting 200 GW of annual solar manufacturing for space:

That's roughly 40% of average US electricity consumption. Its Starmind compute unit delivers the same capability at roughly a quarter the size of a Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, which is a win in space. Elon says it's also simpler than Starlink V3, which is already in production.

Simply put, SpaceX is building toward a trillion-dollar annual revenue business within just a few years, at scale never seen before.

Many of these numbers I've already modeled and shared over the past few months. Yesterday's announcements bring those projections closer to reality.

The scale of what's coming is extraordinary!

Elon Musk says SpaceX’s StarMind orbital AI satellite is a “much easier” engineering problem than Starlink V3:

“I’m not sure why people think that making an AI satellite would be hard, given that SpaceX already has over 11,000 satellites in orbit, which is, I think, twice as much as the rest of the world combined.”

“The StarMind satellite, which is the name for our overall compute system, is simpler, not harder than, say, the Starlink V3 communication satellite, which is an incredibly complex orbital radio station.”

“It’s got the most advanced phased array antennas that have ever been made, far more advanced than anything that any military has at any price.”

“Compared to that, the AI satellite is much, much easier, because it really just consists of a very large array of solar panels and a radiator.”

“You’re gonna have about five times as much solar panel area as you will have radiator area. And that’s just basic physics.”

“Then you have the star computer at the center, which would be physically about a quarter of the size of, say, a Vera Rubin NVL rack while having all of the capability of a Vera Rubin NVL72.”

“I can’t emphasize enough that the StarMind satellite is a much easier technical problem than Starlink V3 communication satellite. I’m not saying it’s trivial, but it’s not as hard as what we’re already doing.”

Elon Musk reveals how Starlink saved Ukraine from collapse, and sets the record straight on claims he throttled it:

“There is no private individual who has helped Ukraine more than I have. I made sure that Starlink was in Ukraine, prepositioned ahead of the Russian invasion.”

“When Russia invaded, they disabled all communications, all cell towers, all fiber cables, and every satellite communication system. There was one system they could not disable, and that was Starlink.”

“If they had not had Starlink, their entire line would have collapsed because they had no communication system, and Russia would have won. Now, does that sound like a pro-Russian action to you?”

“Even to this present day, Starlink provides the backbone of communications for the Ukrainian military and for Ukraine more broadly. If we were to turn off Starlink, the entire Ukrainian front would collapse immediately.”

“From the beginning, I said that Starlink is a civilian system. It is not meant to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people. If you want to do that, you need to do Starshield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the US government.”

“In the Starlink system, there is a speed limit. That speed limit is the speed of the fastest road speed limit in Ukraine, which I think is about 80 miles an hour.”

“Do not ask me as a private individual to make kill decisions that sometimes result in the loss of innocent lives, not just soldiers. That is not my position to do. And yet we’ve been pressed relentlessly to do that, which I think is outrageous.”

“Those are the rules that have been in place since the beginning, for years. Now people pressure me to change it, but I’m not changing it.”

Elon Musk reveals over 30 people now have a Neuralink, some use it to feed themselves with a robot arm, and he's confident it will eventually let people with spinal injuries walk again

"Yeah. So Neuralink, by the way, is obviously, as you mentioned, a private company, much, much smaller. I mean, it's just several hundred people. We now have, I think, over 30 people that have received the Neuralink device. So they have a Neuralink in their head."

"Our focus initially was giving people who are tetraplegics, quadriplegics, the ability to control their phone or their computer or a robot arm just by thinking. So we call that product Telepathy. So just by thinking, you can control a computer or a robot arm. Some of our customers will literally control a robot arm, and they will actually feed themselves. It gives them the power. I mean, imagine you're tetraplegic. You can't do anything. You can't feed yourself. But now, just by thinking, with the robot arm, you can actually feed yourself with the robot arm."

"And how much better… These things that we take for granted are life-changing. And down the road, we feel at this point confident in saying that we'll be able to bridge the signals from the brain, from the motor and sensory cortex, past where the neural damage is from a broken neck or spine, and enable people to walk again."

“If you look into the future, orbital compute is really going to be where things scale to.”

“In the future, the amount of superintelligence compute that is on Earth will round down to 0% and superintelligence compute in space will round up to 100%.”

“Now remember these words, because that sounds like a preposterous thing to say.”

“I think superintelligence compute [on Earth] will be less than 0.4% of compute. Therefore, orbital compute will round up to 100%. And I think this is a relatively easy prediction to make, and it’s simply a matter of time before that happens.”

“Probably yes. Now, this is not like let’s merge the companies no matter what. These require shareholder votes, which may or may not succeed, at least in the case of Tesla.”

“I can’t just drag them into a non-economic merger that is bad for them, because I’ll obviously get sued.”

“It really is just a question of, do SpaceX and Tesla execute better together and create more value than if they’re apart?”

Elon Musk reveals what really drives him to make humanity a star-faring civilization: “It’s life insurance, but for everything.”

“If you simply look at the fossil record and look at how many extinction events have happened, which is a lot, then you know that this is simply a matter of time. It’s a when, not an if.”

“It’s important to have insurance for life as a whole. It’s life insurance, but for everything.”

But what motivates him even more:

“I want to envision a future that’s exciting, that we’re out there exploring new frontiers, going to new star systems, and make science fiction not just fiction forever.”

“We should boldly go like Star Trek, boldly go where no one’s gone before. And perhaps we find some long dead alien civilizations, or perhaps we find actual aliens we could talk to.”

“You know how you can figure out if something’s really cool about the future? Just ask your kid, and they’ll tell you.”

“Life cannot just be about solving one miserable problem after another. There have to be things that excite you and inspire you about the future, that make you happy when you wake up in the morning.”

“You can’t wait to see what happens next. And being a star-faring civilization is one of those things.”

The answer was simpler than anyone expected. They were both the kind of person who makes jokes about obscure AI philosophy at 2am and thinks that's normal. They didn't find each other through fame or fortune. They found each other through a thought experiment that maybe a thousand other people on Earth would have understood.

The rarest kind of connection isn't physical attraction. It's finding someone whose mind works like yours in a world that doesn't understand either of you.

Transformers have barely changed since the 1890s: copper coils in a tank of oil.

Batteries, solar and compute run on DC. The grid runs on AC. Bridging the two has meant inverters plus transformers.

Powercore is a solid-state transformer, breaker and inverter in one box. Finally, one conversion and about half the losses.

Hats off to the Tesla power electronics engineers!
